capabilities.description: Exercise a user-facing web interface through a real browser without prescribing product routes, selectors, or application architecture.
requirements: A repository-owned browser test command and any required service startup belong in the consumer repository.

implementations.name: Playwright
implementations.guidance: Recommended example for browser E2E because it supports modern browsers, traces, screenshots, and deterministic headless execution.

implementations.name: Selenium/WebDriver
implementations.guidance: Use when the consumer already owns WebDriver-based tests or needs a different browser-driver ecosystem.

implementations.name: repository-defined browser runner
implementations.guidance: Any command is valid when it satisfies the browser capability and emits a process exit status suitable for validation evidence.

capabilities.description: Exercise HTTP request/response contracts against a real or controlled service endpoint without prescribing service architecture.
requirements: The consumer owns endpoint configuration, fixtures, credentials, and contract assertions.

implementations.name: Hurl
implementations.guidance: Recommended example for concise executable HTTP request/response contracts.

implementations.name: Schemathesis or OpenAPI-driven runner
implementations.guidance: Use when validation should derive cases from an API schema rather than hand-authored request files.

implementations.name: repository-defined HTTP runner
implementations.guidance: Any command is valid when it exercises the intended HTTP contract and returns a deterministic process result.

capabilities.description: Exercise integration behavior against disposable containerized dependencies such as databases, queues, or service doubles without prescribing a specific product topology.
requirements: A compatible local/container runtime must be available to the consumer execution environment.

implementations.name: Testcontainers
implementations.guidance: Recommended example when tests should create and dispose dependency containers programmatically.

implementations.name: Docker Compose or compatible compose runner
implementations.guidance: Use when the repository already models integration dependencies declaratively and owns lifecycle cleanup.

implementations.name: repository-defined container runner
implementations.guidance: Any command is valid when container lifecycle is bounded, cleanup is reliable, and test exit status is deterministic.
